segments.title: Setting up the recording and giving names
segments.summary: Allen tests the recorder, the date (3 August 1978) is given, and Hall and Albert give their names; Don Albert Dominique.

segments.title: Herbert Hall's birthplace and birth date
segments.summary: Hall says he was born in Reserve, Louisiana, on March 20, 1907.

segments.title: Marshall Lawrence and Kid Thomas
segments.summary: Allen says they need not cover Marshall Lawrence and Kid Thomas; Albert knew Lawrence and Thomas's father.

segments.chapter: Baton Rouge and the Albert band
segments.title: Why Hall joined Albert's band; gigs with Sidney Desvigne
segments.summary: Hall left for adventure as a single man and played only a few gigs with Desvigne; he spent little time in New Orleans.

segments.chapter: Baton Rouge and the Albert band
segments.title: Baton Rouge musicians and the local scene
segments.summary: Allen asks about Kid Victor, John Handy, Bob Thomas, Tutts Johnson, Dimes Weston and bands in Baton Rouge and Reserve.

segments.chapter: Baton Rouge and the Albert band
segments.title: Reed section and instruments in Albert's band
segments.summary: Hall played lead alto, baritone, soprano and clarinet in a three-reed band; he mostly soloed on baritone.

segments.title: Changing style between instruments; Ellington baritone models
segments.summary: Hall says each instrument changes how you play; they listened to Harry Carney, Bigard and Hodges, and Albert says Hall sounded like Carney.

segments.title: Big bands versus small groups
segments.summary: Hall loved big-band sound then but now prefers small groups because arranged bands are restrictive.

segments.title: Hall's arranging by ear and transposing
segments.summary: Hall wrote arrangements from ear with no piano; Albert mentions Lloyd Glenn and Billy Douglas arranging from their heads.

segments.title: Reed section seating and soprano parts
segments.summary: Who played first, second and third parts in the section, doubling on clarinet and soprano, and the vanished soprano sound.

segments.title: Forming the band for Dallas in 1929
segments.summary: The band was assembled in New Orleans for Albert's Dallas job in October 1929; the men travelled in three cars, and Jack was taken on for his transportation.

segments.title: Original personnel: Ten Pals, bass, drums, piano
segments.summary: The band picked up Adam Hardy and Henry Turner in Dallas, added bass (Jimmy Johnson) and drummer Fats Martin, and Al Freeman on piano.

segments.title: Stock arrangements from a Dallas hotel band
segments.summary: A white band at the Adolphus Hotel gave Albert's band a trunk of stock arrangements; Herman Waldman's band played the Baker Hotel.

segments.title: Band members' nicknames
segments.summary: Shook, Nick for Henry Turner and Freeman: nicknames in the band.

segments.title: Touring the Northeast and the weather
segments.summary: They played all over, including upstate New York, Vermont and Albany; Allen asks about weather and Canada.

segments.title: Road conditions: mud roads, pushing the bus
segments.summary: Long jumps over unpaved roads, rocks under the wheels, the hot motor in Virginia mountains, running out of money.

segments.title: Hall leaves the band; the Cincinnati breakup and social security card
segments.summary: Hall left for a year, rejoined, and stayed in Cincinnati when the band broke up; his card shows 1938.

segments.title: Receiving mail on the road via general delivery
segments.summary: The band had no headquarters; mail went by general delivery and Albert's wife collected it.

segments.title: Don Albert's wife
segments.summary: Albert met his wife in New Orleans, not on the road; she has been wonderful.

segments.title: Cities and states toured: Washington, Philadelphia, Midwest
segments.summary: Howard Theater, Philadelphia home base, New Jersey, New York state, Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana.

segments.title: Blues pickers: Blind Lemon, Lead Belly, defining the blues
segments.summary: Albert met Blind Lemon and Lead Belly in east Texas joints and defines the blues as feeling from slavery.

segments.title: Boogie woogie
segments.summary: Albert says boogie woogie was created by piano players and his band played some.

segments.title: Jug bands, kazoo, washboards and string bands
segments.summary: Jug bands only in New Orleans; Bob Burns's instrument came from there; Albert played mandolin, guitar and banjo.

segments.title: Fish fries, penny parties and local food
segments.summary: Catfish fries, French bread, beer, snapping turtle and penny parties.

segments.title: Flash floods and the West
segments.summary: A flash flood in Virginia; the band never went west to Albuquerque.

segments.title: Movies, early records and radio listening
segments.summary: Hearing records at others' houses and radio bands; Duke Ellington was always his band, and trumpeters Bunny and Ziggy.

segments.title: Crescent Bed Factory, Joey Cola and Chinatown
segments.summary: Allen asks about the Crescent Bed Factory, Joey Cola, Tulane Avenue's Chinatown, Chinese cookies and food.

segments.title: Cigar makers, Mr. Morial, work songs and Chris Kelly
segments.summary: Albert's father's cigar workers, Mr. Morial, the singing of workers and washerwomen and Chris Kelly's favorite number.

segments.title: Albert's mother and siblings
segments.summary: His mother Georgiana was a housewife; the order of his siblings and Leo's much later birth.

segments.title: New Orleans baseball and sports
segments.summary: Baseball teams in New Orleans, the Homestead Grays, favorite players and the city's sports decline.

segments.title: Albert's sister and politics
segments.summary: Allen mentions Albert's sister's political activity and campaign stickers.

segments.title: Robichaux family and Tanglefoot
segments.summary: The Robichaux bandleaders John and Joe, the trumpeter Mutt, and a garbled nickname passage.

segments.title: Kimball, listening to whole bands, and end of the reel
segments.summary: Albert asks about trumpeter Kimball and Alvin Alcorn, says he listens to the whole band, and the reel ends.
